oneLiner: 横排为周期（电子层数相同），纵列为族（最外层电子数相同）。
oneLinerEn: Rows are periods (same shells); columns are groups (same valence electrons).
detail: 现有 7 个周期、18 个纵列；主族（IA–VIIA）与副族（过渡金属）性质各异。
detailEn: Seven periods and 18 columns; main groups and transition metals differ in behavior.

oneLiner: 从左到右原子半径减小、金属性减弱、非金属性增强。
oneLinerEn: Left to right: radius shrinks, metallic character weakens, nonmetals strengthen.
detail: 核电荷数增大使原子对电子吸引更强，故失电子能力减弱、得电子能力增强。
detailEn: Rising nuclear charge tightens the pull on electrons, weakening loss and easing gain.

oneLiner: 从上到下原子半径增大、金属性增强、非金属性减弱。
oneLinerEn: Top to bottom: radius grows, metallic character strengthens, nonmetals weaken.
detail: 电子层数增多使外层电子离核更远，更易失去。
detailEn: Extra shells move valence electrons farther, easing their loss.

oneLiner: 金属性指失电子能力，非金属性指得电子能力；分界线附近为类金属。
oneLinerEn: Metallic = losing electrons; nonmetallic = gaining; metalloids sit near the divide.
detail: 左下角（如铯、钫）金属性最强，右上角（如氟）非金属性最强。
detailEn: Strongest metals bottom-left (Cs, Fr); strongest nonmetal top-right (F).

oneLiner: 同周期减小、同主族增大；稀有气体因计量方式通常单独较大。
oneLinerEn: Shrinks across a period, grows down a group; noble-gas values differ by convention.
detail: 原子半径不是实测的硬边，而是把相邻原子核间距取一半推出来的，所以比较时必须守住同一套口径。规律只有两句：同周期从左到右逐渐减小，同主族从上到下逐渐增大。前者是因为电子都填进同一层、屏蔽几乎不增，而核电荷一步步加大，外层被拉得更紧；后者是因为每往下就多出整整一个电子层，层数的作用压过了核电荷的增加。两个常考的比较：一、比微粒半径先看电子层数，层多则大；层数相同再看核电荷，核大则小（O²⁻、F⁻、Na⁺、Mg²⁺、Al³⁺ 都是 2、8 结构，只差质子数，所以依次缩小）。二、同种元素的原子与离子，阳离子一定小于原子（少了一层），阴离子一定大于原子（层没变而电子间斥力变大），所以 Na⁺ 小于 Na、Cl⁻ 大于 Cl。稀有气体要单独说明：它的半径是范德华半径，与相邻元素的金属或共价半径不是同一口径，因此画在同一张折线图上常常突然变大，中学阶段一般不参与比较。
detailEn: An atomic radius is not a measured hard edge: it comes from halving the distance between neighbouring nuclei, so every comparison has to stay inside one convention. The rule is two sentences — radii shrink across a period and grow down a group. In the first case the electrons go into the same shell and screening barely rises while the nuclear charge does, so the outer electrons are pulled tighter; in the second a whole new shell is added, and shell count beats nuclear charge. Two comparisons are examined every year. Particles with different shell counts are ranked by shells first, and where the shell structure is identical the larger nuclear charge wins — O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺, Mg²⁺, Al³⁺ are all 2,8 and shrink in that order. For one element the cation is always smaller than the atom (a shell gone) while the anion is larger (same shell, more electron repulsion), so Na⁺ is under Na and Cl⁻ over Cl. Note the convention clash for noble gases: their figure is a van der Waals radius, not a metallic or covalent one, which is why they jump at the end of a plot and why the school course leaves them out of the ranking.

oneLiner: 电负性衡量吸引共用电子能力（氟最大）；电离能是失电子所需能量。
oneLinerEn: Electronegativity gauges electron attraction (F largest); ionization energy is to remove an electron.
detail: 二者同周期递增、同主族递减；稀有气体电离能出现反常。
detailEn: Both rise across a period and fall down a group; noble gases are exceptions.

oneLiner: 周期表中部 d 区元素，多为有色、可变价、易形成配合物。
oneLinerEn: Central d-block elements: often colored, multiple valences, complex-forming.
detail: 铁、铜、锌等是生命与工业的重要过渡金属。
detailEn: Fe, Cu, Zn are vital transition metals in life and industry.

oneLiner: 最外层电子已满，化学性质极稳定，过去称惰性气体。
oneLinerEn: Filled outer shells make them extremely stable, once called inert gases.
detail: 氦、氖、氩、氪、氙、氡；可用于保护气、照明与制冷。
detailEn: He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn; used as shielding gas, lighting and cooling.
